transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

...I guess I came in because of my husband's sister. I don't really like talking about family business with strangers, but... she's been working things behind the scenes so she can get control of the money. She's trying to push me out of the decisions. 

Folks around us keep trying to smooth it over, tell me I'm wrong, but... I know what I’ve been seeing. It's been going on for more than a year now.
Are you certain that your husband's sister is trying to take control of the money?
Yes. I... I wouldn't say it if I wasn't. Like I just told you, I know what I've been seeing. Everyone else can try to smooth it over all they want, but... it's been over a year of this. I'm sure.
Do you ever hear voices when no one else is around?
No. I don't hear anything like that. Just... regular things.
Do you believe anyone can put thoughts into your mind or take thoughts out of it?
No. I don't... I don't know why you'd ask that. Nobody can do that. My thoughts are just mine.
Before all this with your husband's sister, have you generally found it hard to trust other people?
No. Not really. I... I trusted people fine before. Just normal, I guess. It's just... what she's doing now.
Because of this situation, has your ability to manage your daily life gotten worse?

No, not really. I still do my usual routines... go to church, things like that. 

I guess I just... I've skipped a few family get-togethers lately. And I keep my plans to myself now, mostly about money. I just don't want any of my business getting back to his sister. But other than that, I manage fine.
Have you noticed yourself becoming emotionally flat or less able to feel or show emotions lately?
No. I don't think so. I feel things the same as I always have. I'm just... trying to get by.
Aside from your concerns about your husband's sister and the money, have you had any other beliefs that other people say are untrue or hard to believe?
No. I don't... nothing like that. Just what I already told you about her. That's all.
Have other people told you that the way you speak is hard to follow or doesn’t make sense?
No. No one's said that to me. I speak just fine.
Have you found yourself having much less motivation to do things than you used to?
No. I still do what I need to do every day. Nothing's really changed there.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a single, fixed persecutory belief that her husband's sister has been trying to gain control of family money for over a year, with strong conviction despite others disagreeing. There are no hallucinations, thought insertion/withdrawal, disorganized speech, negative symptoms, or marked deterioration in overall functioning. The belief is non-bizarre, circumscribed, and persistent, which is most consistent with persistent delusional disorder.
